edges.reason: T02's production code imports app/rotation.py and its wiring tests (A1, A2) execute the real rotation functions created by T01 — a concrete file dependency, not just a contract read, so T02 runs after T01.
T03 exists to verify T01 end-to-end: its e2e scenarios drive the rotation module's C1/C3 behavior (naming, retention, compression) through LogWriter and assert the observable file layout.
T03 exists to verify T02: its e2e runs serve() plus the unmodified pre-existing tests against the LogWriter wiring, and it owns seam-defect fixes inside T02's owned files (owns_fixes_for).

fake_serialization_removed.why_not_real: Task statement lists rotation, then retention, then compression as separate bullets; a naive reading could order the wiring (T02) before or alongside the module (T01) by doc order. All three bullets live inside one closure, T01 — no task edge is created from bullet order. The only real leaf edge is T01→T02 (data): T02 imports T01's module in production code, and coding against a test fake would leave T02 unrunnable until T01 lands anyway, for a leaf small enough that the parallelism gain is negative.

collisions_handled: app/logger.py is a known shared file (snapshot known_shared_files): assigned to exactly one owner, T02; T01's forbidden_scope names it and C1 forbids the rotation module importing it, so no ownership collision exists.
free_parallelism_trades: T02 could in principle run in parallel against frozen C1 with a monkeypatched rotation module, but T02's production import and its A1/A2 wiring tests need the real module; serializing one ~30-60 min leaf to keep the tests honest is the cheaper trade for a 2-leaf plan.
T03 is alone in its group (last): it consumes both leaves' outputs; adding it to an earlier group would violate the verification ordering.

contract_bindings.rationale: T01 owns app/rotation.py, the file that defines the C1 interface (service layer per snapshot); T02 imports it for the LogWriter hooks and T03's e2e exercises it through LogWriter.
C2 is the invariant LogWriter interface; T02 owns app/logger.py and must keep the interface unchanged while adding hooks; T03's e2e runs serve() and the pre-existing unmodified tests against it.

The naming/retention/compression policy (C3) is implemented in app/rotation.py by T01; T02's hooks must honor it when calling rotate/apply_retention and T03 asserts its observable file layout end-to-end.

seam_bindings.rationale: S1 is LogWriter ↔ rotation module: T01 owns the module side (app/rotation.py) and T02 owns the writer side (app/logger.py trigger points in __init__ and append); T03 verifies the seam end-to-end and owns seam-defect fixes for both.

S2 is LogWriter ↔ consumers: T02 maintains the invariant interface consumed by the unmodified serve loop (lifecycle side, app/server.py stays untouched) and T03 exercises it through serve() plus the unmodified pre-existing tests (e2e side).
